title: Lycopodium japonicum Thunb. inhibits chondrocyte apoptosis, senescence and inflammation in osteoarthritis through STING/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Ma, Jiawei; Zhang, Hanwen; Wang, Ze; Xu, Cong; Tan, Hongye; Sun, Yun; Zheng, Rukang; Jin, Zebin; Li, Yuanyuan; Ge, Xinjiang; Wu, Yaosen; Zhou, Yifei
one_liner_zh: 研究中药LJT通过STING/NF-kB通路抑制骨关节炎软骨细胞凋亡与炎症，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disease, its characteristic lies in the inflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, can lead to significant personal disability and social burden. Lycopodium japonicum Thunb. (LJT) is a lycopinaceae plant with anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects. In traditional Oriental medicine, LJT is commonly used to treat a variety of conditions, including osteoarthritis and low back pain. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the anti-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory and anti-senescence properties of LJT in IL-1beta-induced mouse chondrocytes, and to clarify the underlying mechanisms involved. In addition, the study also examined the effects of LJT by establishing a mouse model of osteoarthritis. The ultimate goal is to identify the mechanism of LJT as an anti-osteoarthritis agent. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this research, molecular docking and network pharmacology analysis were performed to identify the latent pathways and key targets of LJT action. The CCK-8 kit was used to evaluate LJT's effect on chondrocyte viability. Western blotting, Immunofluorescence, TUNEL staining kit, and SA-beta-gal staining were employed to verify LJT's impact on chondrocytes. Additionally, SO, HE, and Immunohistochemical were utilized to assess LJT's effects on osteoarthritis in mice. In vitro and in vivo experiments were performed to verify the potential mechanism of LJT in OA. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis revealed that AKT1, PTGS2, and ESR1 were the key candidate targets for the treatment of OA with LJT. The results of molecular docking indicated that AKT1 exhibited a low binding affinity to the principal constituents of LJT. Hence, we have chosen STING, an upstream regulator of PTGS2, as our target for investigation. Molecular docking revealed that sitosterol, formononetin, stigmasterol and alpha-Onocerin, the main components of LJT, have good binding activity with STING. In vitro experiments showed that LJT inhibited IL-1beta-mediated secretion of inflammatory mediators, apoptosis and senescence of chondrocytes. The results showed that LJT abolished cartilage degeneration induced by unstable medial meniscus (DMM) in mice. Mechanism research has shown that LJT by inhibiting the STING/NF-kappaB signaling pathways, down-regulating the NF-kappaB activation, so as to inhibit the development of OA. CONCLUSION: LJT reversed the progression of OA by inhibiting inflammation, apoptosis and senescence in animal models and chondrocytes. The effects of LJT are mediated through the STING/NF-kappaB pathway.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：骨关节炎（OA）是一种退行性疾病，其特征为炎症和细胞外基质（ECM）降解，可导致显著的个人残疾和社会负担。石松（Lycopodium japonicum Thunb.，LJT）是一种石松科植物，具有抗炎和镇痛作用。在传统东方医学中，LJT常用于治疗多种疾病，包括骨关节炎和腰痛。研究目的：探讨LJT在IL-1β诱导的小鼠软骨细胞中的抗凋亡、抗炎和抗衰老特性，并阐明其潜在机制。此外，本研究还通过建立小鼠骨关节炎模型来考察LJT的作用。最终目标是明确LJT作为抗骨关节炎药物的作用机制。材料与方法：本研究采用分子对接和网络药理学分析，以识别LJT作用的潜在通路和关键靶点。使用CCK-8试剂盒评估LJT对软骨细胞活力的影响。采用Western blotting、免疫荧光、TUNEL染色试剂盒和SA-β-gal染色验证LJT对软骨细胞的作用。此外，利用SO、HE和免疫组织化学方法评估LJT对小鼠骨关节炎的影响。通过体外和体内实验验证LJT在OA中的潜在机制。结果：网络药理学分析显示，AKT1、PTGS2和ESR1是LJT治疗OA的关键候选靶点。分子对接结果表明，AKT1与LJT主要成分的结合亲和力较低。因此，我们选择PTGS2的上游调控因子STING作为研究靶点。分子对接显示，LJT的主要成分谷甾醇、芒柄花素、豆甾醇和α-芒柄花素与STING具有良好的结合活性。体外实验表明，LJT抑制了IL-1β介导的炎症介质分泌、软骨细胞凋亡和衰老。结果显示，LJT消除了小鼠内侧半月板不稳定（DMM）诱导的软骨退化。机制研究表明，LJT通过抑制STING/NF-κB信号通路，下调NF-κB激活，从而抑制OA的发展。结论：LJT通过抑制炎症、凋亡和衰老，在动物模型和软骨细胞中逆转了OA的进展。LJT的作用通过STING/NF-κB通路介导。
